default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-009.title: Pin-bar rejection
E-009.hypothesis: A bar of at least typical range with a small body and a long wick on one side shows that aggressive orders pushed the price there and were absorbed by resting liquidity; the absorbed side is exhausted, follow the close away from the wick.

E-010.title: Strong-close bar follow
E-010.hypothesis: A bar of typical-or-larger range that is almost all body and closes at its extreme means aggressive orders were still being filled at the bell of the bar; a parent order still being worked continues into the next bars, so follow it.

E-011.title: Break-and-retest
E-011.hypothesis: After a close beyond the recent high/low, a pullback that touches the broken level and closes back on the breakout side shows old resistance acting as support (late sellers covering, missed buyers stepping in); enter on the retest rather than the break.

E-012.title: Close-location flow divergence
E-012.hypothesis: A new recent low while the volume-weighted close location of the same window is positive means bars keep closing high on volume: passive buyers absorb the sellers making the low; fade the extreme.

E-013.title: Session extreme after a pause
E-013.hypothesis: When the session high/low has stood untouched for a long time, stops and breakout orders pile up beyond it; the first close through it after the pause releases them, follow the break.

E-014.title: Engulfing reversal after a run
E-014.hypothesis: After several consecutive closes in one direction, a bar that reverses and closes beyond the previous bar's extreme shows the short-term momentum traders are trapped and the other side took control; follow the reversal.

E-015.title: Late-day trend breakout
E-015.hypothesis: Late-informed traders and rebalancers finish their orders near the close in the direction of the day; in the last hour or two, on a day already moving more than usual, follow a break of the 15-minute high/low in the day's direction.

E-016.title: Double test that holds
E-016.hypothesis: A return to the recent low (high) after moving away, that does not break it and closes in the bounce direction, shows resting orders still defend the level and sellers cannot push through; trade the hold.

E-017.title: Flag after an impulse bar
E-017.hypothesis: A large impulse bar followed by small bars that hold its far half means the impulse side is not being unwound; a close beyond the impulse bar's extreme resumes the move as the pause traders give up.

E-018.title: Swing-structure break
E-018.hypothesis: After a higher swing low (lower swing high), a close through the last swing high (low) completes an intraday trend structure that swing traders watch; their entries and the stops of the counter side push it on.
